messages:
Priya S.: quick heads-up  opened a tiny docs PR to correct a couple of observability examples and add a short note under the cost table. pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999 :wave:
Omar L.: thanks. which examples?
Priya S.: tracing hook examples (Python + Node) and the kv-cache snippet in the dashboard tutorial. also adding a 1-line non-technical note: 'Shorter average sequences usually lower per-token cost due to better batching.'
Casey W.: can you also change the dashboard filter example to use `trace_id` (snake_case)? saw `traceId` in one place. small consistency thing.
Priya S.: yep will fix to `trace_id`.
Omar L.: small nit  Node snippet missing `await fetchTrace()` so playground shows an empty trace.
Casey W.: I pushed a 1-line await fix and updated the codeblock language to `javascript` so highlighting is right.
Priya S.: thanks Casey. also swapped kv example from manual prefixing to helper API:
```js
// before
const key = `sess:${sessionId}:kv`
await kv.set(key, payload)
// after
await kv.setForSession(sessionId, payload)
```
Priya S.: keeps customers from copying internal prefix patterns.
Omar L.: nice. one more thing: the PR links to `/sdk/node/legacy` in two places  legacy path is deprecated, please replace with `/sdk/node/current`.
Priya S.: good catch, will replace those links.
docs-bot: docs CI succeeded for PR #4999 (build 4812) :white_check_mark:
Omar L.: reviewed and left :+1: for the await + kv helper change. asked for a tiny variable-name tweak (`sessId` -> `sessionId`) in one commit.
Casey W.: fixed the var name and squashed a lint bot commit. re-approved.
Priya S.: final checklist: 1) replace legacy links 2) squash if needed 3) merge after approvals. anyone block merging?
Omar L.: no blockers from me.
Casey W.: go for merge.
Priya S.: merging in a bit. tagging #product-docs for visibility :sparkles:
__notes: Slack thread coordinating a docs PR: tracing hook and kv-cache snippet fixes, await and variable-name fixes, link replacement, short cost/latency note, CI pass. Messages kept short and Slack-like.
